label: Exceeded-god rival of God's maximality in being survives, checked
description: Rival test for God's maximality in being against its smallest consumer, StageTwo.GodIsSimple.godIsSimple (premises: whatever is God is maximal in being, every composite has a uniting cause of its esse, a cause of a quality in another is more such). With a composite god whose uniting cause is more in being and is not God, the exceeded-god rival holds with the other two premises and God is composite. Model-witnessed survival only; it does not show that the name God is correctly applied to such a being.

research_comparisons.conditions: Control.demiurgeGod, demiurgeAct, demiurgeMore, demiurgeCause, with Composite := demiurgeGod: the rival, CompositeHasAUnitingCauseReading and CauseOfQualityInAnotherIsMoreSuchReading hold; GodIsSimple fails. Consumer tested: StageTwo.GodIsSimple.godIsSimple.
research_comparisons.scope: Same IsGod, InAct, MoreIn and esse as the premise; two members, one respect.
research_comparisons.coverage: One explicitly populated interpretation; not every finite-god theology.
research_comparisons.exclusivity: The rival and the premise cannot both hold on one IsGod, InAct, MoreIn and esse (unregistered helper exceededGod_excludes).
research_comparisons.witness: Control.demiurgeGod with demiurgeAct, demiurgeMore, demiurgeCause in Control.ExceededGodSurvives; exceededGodSurvives proves the listed conjuncts.
research_comparisons.next_step: Test the rival against the nominal definitions of stage one: under 'God names what is maximal in being' the exceeding thing, if maximal, is God, which the rival denies.
